propositions: The CLI write-command argument parsing uses hand-rolled loops (_parse_force, _parse_assignee, _parse_flags) with bespoke semantics (--assignee absent=None vs empty='', --force bare vs =reason) that must be migrated to stdlib argparse without changing observable behavior.

Argparse defaults conflict with required behaviors: unknown tokens must be silently skipped (parse_known_args, not parse_args), --help must remain dispatcher-served from golden files (add_help=False), abbreviations must be disabled (allow_abbrev=False), and argparse's exit-2 errors must become exit-1 CommandError.

The transition._parse_flags 5-tuple shim must be retained with identical None-vs-'' semantics and retired --force-close rejection for three external direct callers (test_close_ref_target_80af, test_transition_force_flag_24f7, test_dependency_audit) to pass unchanged.

The --force semantics differ per command: claim bare --force consumes next non-option token else '(no reason given)', but transition bare --force sets force_reason='' (not '') and never consumes following tokens, with _force_note mapping '' to '(no reason given)' to preserve observable behavior.

The --assignee None-vs-'' distinction must be preserved: --assignee absent triggers default_assignee fallback, explicit --assignee '' clears it, and --assignee value-less exits 1; both inline (--assignee=value) and space-separated (--assignee value) forms must be accepted.
Module-size and complexity ratchets must be respected: transition ≤707 LOC, claim ≤350 LOC, _seam ≤625 LOC, with _parse_flags complexity dropping below threshold to drain its stale baseline entry.
